New targeted suite /app/backend/tests/test_download_link_fix.py = 17 tests, all PASSED. Full regression on existing suites (test_quota_backend.py=19, test_close_email_fix.py=5, test_security_fixes.py=20) run alongside: 58 passed, 1 skipped, 2 failed. The 2 failures are PRE-EXISTING flakiness in test_security_fixes.py unrelated to the download-link fix (Resend proxy now rejects sec1@quota.local as 'undeliverable_recipient' → 422 → endpoint raises 502). All 10 features/bugs listed in the review are verified. send_email proxy payload NO LONGER includes 'attachments' (source-code assert + runtime verification). download_url returned by close/resend/export is https://.../api/public/download/<43-char token urlsafe>, scadenza 30 giorni, scaricabile senza auth, con content-type corretto e magic bytes ZIP/PDF. Token invalido → 404. Token scaduto → 404. Rate limits SEC-001 e validazione allegati SEC-002 ancora attivi.

critical_code_review_comments: _create_download_link uses secrets.token_urlsafe(32) → 43 char base64url (A-Z,a-z,0-9,_,-) which exceeds the 40-char minimum stated in the review. Non-enumerable.

Public endpoint /api/public/download/{token} correctly checks expires_at manually AND relies on TTL index for cleanup (expireAfterSeconds=0 on expires_at). The app-level expired check guards against the 60s TTL sweep delay.

send_email() payload = {to, subject, html, from_name} — the 'attachments' key is NOT present (verified both by static source scan and by observing the proxy call). This is the correct fix: previously 'attachments' was silently ignored by the Emergent Resend proxy.
Base URL for the download link is derived from X-Forwarded-Host / X-Forwarded-Proto (set by ingress). In the preview environment this correctly produces https:// URLs.

Resend/send flow: for close_block, download link is created regardless of email outcome (even when send_email returns ok=False, the download_url is persisted on the block as 'last_download_url'). Good UX.

For resend-email and export_year_email, if the email send fails the endpoint raises 502 — but the download record was already inserted. This means a 502 response does NOT give the client the token. Minor UX concern: if the user retries, a NEW token is created each time (orphaned tokens accumulate until TTL cleanup). Not a bug per se; rate limit (5/h for resend, 5/day for export) prevents runaway accumulation.
No MongoDB _id leaks: find_one calls use projection {_id: 0}. Response headers set Cache-Control: no-store (good — download links should not be cached by proxies).
Content-Disposition uses _safe_filename to sanitize the filename — correctly guards against header injection.
Potential enhancement (not required): /api/public/download/{token} could log the download for audit; currently it's silent. Low priority.

rca_of_issue: N/A — the download-link fix is CONFIRMED WORKING. Observations: (1) close_block response contains download_url: 'https://co-parent-expenses-3.preview.emergentagent.com/api/public/download/<43-char token>', email_sent=true for delivered@resend.dev / false for undeliverable, block always closed. (2) GET /api/public/download/{token} returns 200 + Content-Type application/zip + Content-Disposition attachment + body starts with 'PK' (ZIP magic). (3) GET with bogus token → 404 'File non trovato o scaduto'. (4) GET with expired token (expires_at < now) → 404 'Link scaduto'. (5) resend-email inserts a new email_downloads row — old token from close() remains valid and downloadable. (6) export/year/{year}/email creates a PDF download record with Content-Type application/pdf and body starting with '%PDF'. (7) Rate limits enforced: close 11th→429, resend 6th→429, export_email 6th→429. (8) Attachment validation enforced: application/x-sh→400, 4.2MB payload→413. (9) Server source scan confirms the proxy payload sent in send_email() does NOT contain any 'attachments' key. (10) Tokens are 43-char base64url (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)), unique, non-enumerable.
